papers.what_it_is: A vendor web page listing abstracts of papers, patents and conference items on quantum parametric mode sorting, single-photon lidar and remote sensing, with several abstracts cut short by the page.

assertions.value: The page sits in the Resource library, under Research and publications, of the Quantum Computing Inc website and carries the heading Remote sensing, followed by a list of publications.

assertions.value: The authors report reconstructing the 3D profile of an obscured scene with only 0.0006 detected signal photons per pulse, despite 34-fold spectral-temporally overlapping noise photons within the 6 ps detection window.
assertions.anchor: Noise-tolerant single photon sensitive three-dimensional imager, abstract
quotes: With only 0.0006 detected signal photons per pulse, we reliably reconstruct the 3D profile of an obscured scene, despite 34-fold spectral-temporally overlapping noise photons, within the 6 ps detection window
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, seen here only as an abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: The CLEO 2019 abstract on this page for the same imager gives 50-folds stronger background noise, not 34-fold; the two items may describe different runs or analyses.

assertions.value: The authors state that the 34-fold noise within the 6 ps window amounts to 113,000 times noise per 20 ns detection period.
assertions.anchor: Noise-tolerant single photon sensitive three-dimensional imager, abstract
quotes: despite 34-fold spectral-temporally overlapping noise photons, within the 6 ps detection window
(amounting to 113,000 times noise per 20 ns detection period)
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim in an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum parametric mode sorting can achieve signal to noise exceeding by far what is possible with typical linear optics filters.
assertions.anchor: Noise-tolerant single photon sensitive three-dimensional imager, abstract
quotes: quantum parametric mode sorting (QPMS) can achieve signal to noise exceeding by far what is possible with typical linear optics filters
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim in an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report noise-tolerant 3D imaging with 8 dB noise rejection beyond the theoretical limit of linear-optical matched filters, from only 0.0006 detected signal photons per pulse with 50-folds stronger background noise.
assertions.anchor: Noise-tolerant 3D Imaging, CLEO 2019 abstract
quotes: We demonstrate noise-tolerant 3D imaging with 8 dB noise rejection beyond the theoretical limit of linear-optical matched filters.
We perform the imaging from only 0.0006 detected signal photons per pulse despite being swamped by 50-folds stronger background noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, seen as an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report a 41-dB increase in signal-to-noise ratio for single-photon counting compared with direct detection using a commercial InGaAs single-photon detector, with sub-millimeter ranging resolution and few detected photons.
assertions.anchor: Mode selective up-conversion detection for LIDAR applications, abstract
quotes: We demonstrate a 41-dB increase in the signal-to-noise ratio for single-photon counting compared to that of direct detection using a commercial InGaAs single-photon detector, while achieving sub-millimeter ranging resolution with few detected photons.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, seen as an abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: The baseline is one commercial detector, so the 41 dB is a comparison with that setup, not a general limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that the approach pumps a nonlinear waveguide at the edge of phase matching with picosecond pulses, so that only backscattered signal photons in a single or few desirable time-frequency modes are efficiently up-converted while broadband background noise in other modes is rejected.
assertions.anchor: Mode selective up-conversion detection for LIDAR applications, abstract
quotes: It involves pumping a nonlinear waveguide at the edge of phase matching with picosecond pulses, so that only the backscattered signal photons in a single or few desirable time-frequency modes are efficiently up-converted
assertions.certainty_reason: A description of method in an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report single photon sensitive non-invasive 3D imaging of targets occluded by strongly scattering media with optical thicknesses reaching 9.5l_s (19l_s round trip), and diffraction-limited imaging of a target placed 130 cm away, needing one photon detection out of 50,000 probe pulses.
assertions.anchor: Non-invasive single photon imaging through strongly scattering media, abstract
quotes: we demonstrate single photon sensitive non-invasive 3D imaging of targets occluded by strongly scattering media
optical thicknesses reaching 9.5l_s (19l_s round trip)
diffraction-limited imaging of a target placed 130 cm away through the opaque media
requiring only one photon detection out of 50,000 probe pulses
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, seen as an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that the imaging technique does not require wavefront shaping nor computationally-intensive image reconstruction algorithms.
assertions.anchor: Non-invasive single photon imaging through strongly scattering media, abstract
quotes: Our single photon sensitive imaging technique does not require wavefront shaping nor computationally-intensive image reconstruction algorithms
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim in an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report that selective upconversion of Laguerre-Gaussian spatial modes mixed with turbulent noise reaches ~40 dB extinction without turbulence and maintains ~20 dB in the presence of strong turbulence.
assertions.anchor: Mode selective up-conversion detection with turbulence, abstract
quotes: The extinction reaches ~40 dB without turbulence, and maintains ~20 dB in the presence of strong turbulence.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, seen as an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that they account for turbulence indirectly by modulating only the pump driving the nonlinear process and not the images themselves, using sum frequency generation in a lithium niobate crystal.
assertions.anchor: Mode selective up-conversion detection with turbulence, abstract
quotes: here we account for the turbulence indirectly, by modulating only the pump driving the nonlinear process but not the images themselves
Using specifically sum frequency generation in a lithium niobate crystal
assertions.certainty_reason: A description of method in an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that they propose and demonstrate a photon-efficient optical classifier that overcomes the Rayleigh limit in spatial resolution, using mode-selective sum-frequency generation and single-pixel photon detection.
assertions.anchor: Super-resolution optical classifier with high photon efficiency, abstract
quotes: We propose and demonstrate a photon-efficient optical classifier to overcome the Rayleigh limit in spatial resolution.
It utilizes mode-selective sum-frequency generation and single-pixel photon detection
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim in an abstract.

assertions.anchor: Robust and efficient single-pixel image classification with nonlinear optics, abstract

assertions.value: The authors describe a hybrid image classifier that combines feature-sensitive image upconversion, single pixel photodetection and deep learning, with partial Fourier transform used to extract signature features in both the original and Fourier domains.
assertions.anchor: Robust and efficient single-pixel image classification with nonlinear optics, abstract
quotes: We present a hybrid image classifier by feature-sensitive image upconversion, single pixel photodetection, and deep learning
It uses partial Fourier transform to extract the images' signature features in both the original and Fourier domains
assertions.certainty_reason: A description of method in an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report 94% classification accuracy on MNIST handwritten digits in the presence of 500 times stronger in-band noise than the signal received, using quantum parametric mode sorting with a single-pixel compressive sensing classifier.
assertions.anchor: Noise-Resilient Single-Pixel Compressive Sensing with Single Photon Counting, abstract
quotes: We achieve 94% classification accuracy in the presence of 500 times stronger in-band noise than the signal received.
Using MNIST handwritten digits as an example, we examine the effects of detector dark counts and in-band background noises
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, seen as an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report creating quantum correlated photons in finite-energy Airy transverse modes via spontaneous parametric down conversion and spatial light modulation, and verifying their Airy wavefunctions and parabolic propagation by two-photon coincidence measurements.
assertions.anchor: Quantum Airy photons, abstract
quotes: creating quantum correlated photons in finite-energy Airy transverse modes via spontaneous parametric down conversion and subsequential spatial light modulation
we verify their Airy spatial wavefunctions, propagation along a parabolic trajectory

assertions.value: The authors report that the spatial modulation does not introduce any observable degradation of quantum correlation between the photons.

assertions.value: The authors report that picosecond-gated single photon detection by nonlinear frequency conversion reliably achieves imaging and position retrieval of obscured objects around the corner, and that vibration frequencies of different objects can be resolved from the photon number fluctuation within a ten-picosecond window, allowing NLOS acoustic sensing.
assertions.anchor: Single photon imaging and sensing of highly obscured objects around the corner, abstract
quotes: this approach can reliably achieve imaging and position retrieval of obscured objects around the corner
the vibration frequencies of different objects can be resolved by analyzing the photon number fluctuation received within a ten-picosecond window, allowing NLOS acoustic sensing
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, seen as an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report compressive non-line-of-sight imaging with a downsampling ratio of 6.25% using a convolutional neural network trained purely on a simulated dataset, with photon arrival-time histograms at 10 picosecond resolution.
assertions.anchor: Compressive Non-line-of-sight Imaging using a Convolutional Neural Network, abstract
quotes: We demonstrate compressive non-line-of-sight imaging with downsampling ratio of 6.25% by using a convolutional neural network (CNN).
Photon arrival-time histogram with 10 picosecond resolution enables high-quality image reconstruction with CNN trained purely by using simulated dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, seen as an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that Monte Carlo lidar radiative transfer simulations of ICESat-2 532 nm measurements show the lidar backscattering pathlength follows the Gamma distribution, and that they derive three analytical equations giving snow depth from the average, second- and third-order moments.
assertions.anchor: Deriving snow depth from ICESat-2 LiDAR multiple scattering measurements, abstract
quotes: ICESat-2 measurements of 532 nm laser light propagation in snow
we find that the lidar backscattering pathlength follows the Gamma distribution
we derive three simple analytical equations to compute snow depth from the average, second- and third-order moments of the distribution
assertions.certainty_reason: Theory seen only as an abstract; the statement and conditions are not quoted from the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that ICESat-2 snow depths over Arctic sea ice agree with co-located IceBridge snow radar values with an RMS difference of 7.8 cm or 29.2% of the mean snow depth, and differ from University of Arizona gridded daily snow products by an RMS of 14 cm, or 28% of the mean.
assertions.anchor: Deriving Snow Depth From ICESat-2 Lidar Multiple Scattering Measurements: Uncertainty Analyses, abstract

assertions.value: The authors report simulation results indicating snow depth errors would be less than 5 cm if the standard deviation of pulse spreading due to surface roughness is within 50 cm.
